passes.summary: A rotation day: Nasdaq -1.5% and chips -7% on HPE's margin warning while the Dow closed above 50,000 and health care, staples and retail rose; Dell beat after the close and is up only 2-5%. Most of the screen is either that rotation or a stretched name with nothing dated. Three shorts with a company reason still running are taken: Maximus, Texas Pacific Land and Medtronic. The gateway timed out, so no overnight spreads or sweep; PCE is at 7:30 AM CT.

A 3% liquidation morning (SPY -3.0%, QQQ -4.4%, VIX 33) led by AI and chips, with hot core PCE, a December hike priced near 98% and new tariff proposals; most of the screen is the same beta move seen twice (defensive groups not falling, AI-linked groups falling hardest), so only the two names with their own dated news are taken: Nutanix short on a chief executive exit and Borr long on its founder's largest buy of the year.

A hot October PCE (3.8%, core 3.3%), a hike on 12-9 priced near 98%, a new tariff proposal and a second day of AI-hardware selling: Nasdaq -1.5%, chips -3%, VIX 29, with the Dow, small caps, staples and energy up and the opening lows bought. Three takes, each on news of its own and none on the chip tape: Deere long after a guide miss was bought on 3.7x volume, Jacobs short as a good-looking print is sold harder on day two, Williams long on an informed director's first open-market buy. The other 22 are sector moves with no news of their own, insider buys the price has already left or that a stop could not survive, bounces off lows with no dated event, or read-throughs with no link.
